profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft
profile.summary:
Madeline Nelson is a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft working in the Business Applications Group. She works on the Power Platform Team that supports the licensing for Power Automate, Power BI, and Power Apps, and Microsoft Copilot

Madeline Nelson graduated from Duke University's Pratt School of Engineering in May 2019. She earned a Bachelors of Engineering in Electrical and Computer Engineering, a Bachelors of Science in Computer Science, and a minor in Finance. Madeline has experience as a software engineer intern at Microsoft and Fanatics Inc. and as a content development intern at SmartAction. She also has extensive technical skills and leadership skills which she cultivated over her four years at Duke University.

During the summer of 2018, she worked as a software engineer intern at Microsoft in Redmond, WA. She was part of the CAP Admin Experiences team for Dynamics 365. As an intern she helped design, develop, and deploy a notification service for the team.

During the summer of 2017, her technical skills were further developed as she worked as a software engineer intern for a branded engineering team at Fanatics Inc.

At Duke University, Madeline honed her leadership and organizational skills, and learned the importance of collaboration through her involvement and leadership in Duke Technology Scholars, Business Oriented Women (BOW), Society of Women Engineers (SWE), and Sheroes.

Madeline has volunteered with Special Olympics, Relay for Life, and the YMCA. She coached a youth soccer team through the YMCA during the fall of 2016.

From Sun Valley, Idaho, Madeline is an enthusiastic worker, eager to learn, and always positive.

positions.title: Computer Science & Engineering Tutor
positions.description:
●Tutor 8+ students in Computer Science and Electrical & Computer Engineering.
●Plan, lead, and execute group tutoring sessions and one-on-one sessions weekly,
    teaching Java, C, MATLAB, Python, and MIPS.

positions.title: Co-President of Duke Technology Scholar's Executive Board
positions.description:
The Duke Technology Scholars Program is a comprehensive effort to inspire more Duke women undergraduates to choose careers in computer science and electrical & computer engineering. Its goal is to create a pipeline of women who will thrive in an industry that is the backbone of our society and economy.

The premier Duke female technological organization includes an internship in the SF Bay area, mentorship, networking events, group living, travel to the Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing, and a continued community at Duke.

positions.title: President
positions.description:
● Manage budget of $3,000+ and organize and execute community building events on campus.
● Build connections and develop programs to increase the support system for female engineers and involvement on campus.

positions.title: Technology Committee Member
positions.description:
● Cultivate the careers of BOW women interested in technology and support tech-related projects piloted by BOW women. 
● Participate in skill building workshops, networking events with industry professionals, and guest speaker lectures.  
● Selected through a competitive application and interview process to be a member of Duke’s premier women’s pre-professional organization.

volunteerExperiences.description: Head coach for a soccer team of 3rd and 4th grade students, plan and lead practice every Thursday and a game every Saturday, teaching the students the importance of sportsmanship and being active.

Volunteered with the North Valley Bears Floor Hockey team every Sunday during winter term throughout my Deerfield Career. Practiced with the athletes, recruited volunteers, fundraised and made signs for games.
